title: Fall

rationale.Orthostatic vital signs: SBP drop ≥20, DBP drop ≥10 within 3min standing.
rationale.Non-pharmacologic measures: Fluid/salt, compression stockings, slow position changes.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with recurrent falls, dizziness, lightheadedness, and near-syncope upon standing (within 3 min of standing). Orthostatic hypotension = drop in SBP ≥20mmHg or DBP ≥10mmHg within 3 min of standing. Causes: medications (antihypertensives — especially alpha-blockers, diuretics, nitrates, TCAs, dopaminergics), hypovolemia, autonomic neuropathy (DM, Parkinson's), prolonged bed rest. Workup: orthostatic vital signs, medication review, CBC (anemia), BMP (dehydration, electrolyte), EKG, consider autonomic testing. Treatment: review and adjust medications. Non-pharmacologic: increase fluid/salt intake (if no CHF), compression stockings, elevate head of bed, slow position changes, avoid prolonged standing. If needed: fludrocortisone (mineralocorticoid — expand volume) or midodrine (alpha-1 agonist).
